title: Register comparison run
statement: Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input, let $y$ be a Boolean word, and let $B$ be a natural-number register bound. Suppose the initial register contents $v$ satisfy $v(r)\le B$ for every register $r$ and $v(r_T)=0$. In the register program with mode $\mathrm{mode}$, starting at the comparison instruction, there is a run to the comparison’s next instruction: it reaches the clearing instruction if $v(r_{\mathrm{Pos}})\le v(r_{\mathrm{N1}})$ and the rejecting instruction otherwise, and the resulting registers agree with $v$ except that register $r_T$ contains $\min(v(r_{\mathrm{Pos}}),v(r_{\mathrm{N1}}))$; every configuration before the final one satisfies the run guard with bound $B$.
hypotheses_covered: finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine N over Boolean input
initial register contents v bounded by B at every register
